```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 80)
```

FSNA analyses directed social networks whose ties are triangular fuzzy numbers
(TFNs). It contains the indices of Porreca, Maturo and Ventre (2025), with the
choice of the method used to rank fuzzy numbers, and the exact computation of
fuzzy centralities by the extension principle, with possibilistic comparisons
of the actors.

```{r}
library(FSNA)
```

## Triangular fuzzy numbers

A TFN $(l, m, r)$ has support $[l, r]$ and core $m$. Sums and multiplication
by non-negative scalars act on the three parameters.

```{r}
a <- tfn(c(0.1, 0.3), c(0.5, 0.45), c(0.9, 0.5), names = c("tie 1", "tie 2"))
a
a + a
alpha_cut(a, c(0, 0.5, 1))
sapply(fuzzy_rank_methods(), function(m) tfn_score(a, m))
plot(a)
```

## Fuzzy social networks

A network is stored as three matrices with the left endpoints, the cores and
the right endpoints of the ties (rows: senders, columns: receivers). Absent ties
are null fuzzy numbers. Networks are built from matrices (`fsn()`), from ratings
in long format (`fsn_from_ratings()`), from igraph objects or by simulation.

```{r}
x <- fsn_example()
x
fsn_tie(x, "A", "B")
plot(x, main = "Example network")
```

## A survey network

The questionnaire data of the two departments analysed by Porreca, Maturo and
Ventre (2025) and Porreca and Maturo (2026) are not distributed with the
package; they are available on request (`?fsna_questionnaire`). The examples use
a simulated network with the same structure: only respondents send ties.

```{r}
A <- fsn_simulated()
summary(A)
```

## Indices of Porreca, Maturo and Ventre (2025)

These indices apply the crisp formula to the three parameters of the TFNs and
rank TFNs by their centre of gravity, as described in that paper.

```{r}
print(ijar_degree(A, "in"), n = 5)
print(ijar_closeness(A, "in"), n = 5)
print(ijar_betweenness(A), n = 3)
```

The ranking score can be changed in every function, for example
`rank_method = "graded_mean"`. See `vignette("ijar-indices")`.

## Exact fuzzy centralities

Porreca and Maturo (2026) show that, for an index that is continuous and
non-decreasing in the ties, the $\alpha$-cuts of the fuzzy centrality defined
by the extension principle are obtained exactly from two crisp evaluations per
level.

```{r}
fc <- fuzzy_centrality(A, "in_closeness_prod", max_steps = 2)
fc
plot(fc, actors = 5)
```

Actors are compared by possibility and necessity degrees, certified orderings,
rank intervals and the fuzzy set of the most central actor; see
`vignette("exact-centrality")`.

```{r}
head(summary(fc), 6)
```

## Complete analysis in one call

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- fsna_analyze(A, output_dir = "analysis_A")   # figures, tables, report.html
```

Data collection without mouse tracking is described in
`vignette("data-collection")`.
